Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are making their way out to the middle now. The floodlights are on and the dew has already started to settle in. Hayley Matthews and Qiana Joseph are the two openers for West Indies Women. Renuka Singh Thakur to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, 315 is the number that the West Indies Women will need to get to take this opening game. They have a few explosive batters and the dew coming in should make batting a bit easy. However, it is still a massive total, and with a potent bowling attack, India Women will also feel confident of defending this total. It is going to be a really exciting chase. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

The debutant, Pratika Rawal is up for a quick chat. She expresses pride in representing India, calling it a privilege. She admits feeling nervous initially but credits Smriti Mandhana for easing her into the game and boosting her confidence. Pratika highlights the importance of her role and is pleased with her performance. Says growing up, she admired Smriti’s batting and feels disappointed she missed a well-deserved century. She praises the team's effort, noting every batter contributed to a strong total that should be defendable.

The West Indies Women will be particularly disappointed with their fielding performance, which could end up being the decisive factor in this game. While they were disciplined during the first Powerplay, missed opportunities allowed the hosts to take command. Skipper Hayley Matthews eventually provided the breakthrough, but the team failed to capitalize on it, conceding several crucial partnerships. Misfields and extras further compounded their struggles. Zaida James stood out as the pick of the bowlers with her fantastic five-for, while Matthews claimed two, and Deandra Dottin chipped in with one.

Following the solid start, Smriti Mandhana and Harmanpreet Kaur built on the momentum with a steady 50-run partnership. Unfortunately, Mandhana fell just short of a well-deserved century, departing for 91. The hosts then stitched together a few more crucial partnerships - first between Kaur and Harleen Deol, and later between Kaur and Richa Ghosh, who accelerated the scoring in the death overs. Although both departed, Jemimah Rodrigues and Deepti Sharma ensured the efforts of the top order didn’t go to waste, unleashing an explosive finish to propel the total beyond 300. However, they only managed to add 13 runs in the last 2 overs suffering a mini-collapse in the end.

The Indian openers adopted a cautious approach to get used to the conditions at this brand-new stadium. Debutant Pratika Rawal faced some early struggles and had a stroke of luck when she edged one behind, but the Windies opted not to review. At the other end, Smriti Mandhana showcased her fine form, maintaining a solid scoring rate. She brought up a well-deserved half-century, with the opening partnership contributing 110 runs. Pratika displayed remarkable resilience, transforming her innings from a slow 4 off 24 balls to a composed 40 off 69.

An outstanding batting display from India Women! They could not really finish with a flurry losing 4 wickets for just 12 runs, but still posted a big total on the board. West Indies Women weren't at their best in this game but pulled things back nicely in the end with a magnificent maiden five-wicket haul from Zaida James.
A single in the end takes India Women to 314/9 in their first innings. Fuller on the stumps and Priya Mishra slogs it to long on for one.

After a thrilling conclusion to the 3-match T20I series, the spotlight now shifts to the ODIs! India Women are set to take on West Indies Women in a 3-match series at the Kotambi Stadium in Vadodara. Riding high on momentum after clinching the T20I series with a record-breaking performance smashing 217 runs, their highest total in T20Is, India Women will look to carry their form and start strong in this fresh challenge. While West Indies Women fell short in the T20I series, they displayed plenty of positives to build on, and it's certain that they’ll make life difficult for the hosts. India have made notable changes to their squad for this format. Arundhati Reddy, Shafali Verma, and Radha Yadav miss out, paving the way for maiden call-ups for Pratika Rawal and Tanuja Kanwer. In the batting department, India will once again rely on the experienced trio of Smriti Mandhana, Jemimah Rodrigues and skipper Harmanpreet Kaur to lead the charge. On the bowling front, the new-look attack will revolve around the ever-reliable Renuka Singh Thakur and Deepti Sharma, whose all-round abilities will be key to India’s success. For West Indies Women, Deandra Dottin’s much-anticipated return to the ODI setup will be a major boost. However, they will be without their seasoned campaigner Stafanie Taylor, who is still recovering from an injury. The return of pacer Shabika Gajnabi and wicketkeeper-batter Rashada Williams brings additional depth to the squad. The visitors will bank heavily on Hayley Matthews and Dottin, who are expected to play pivotal roles with both bat and ball. With a capable batting order and a balanced bowling unit featuring Karishma Ramharack, Afy Fletcher and Aaliyah Alleyne, West Indies Women look well-equipped to pose a serious challenge to the home side. This ODI series carries an added sense of history and rivalry. The last time West Indies Women toured India for a white-ball series was in 2016, where they experienced contrasting fortunes, being clean-swept in the ODIs while managing a clean sweep in the T20Is. This time, West Indies will look to rewrite history, riding on their renewed confidence, while India will aim to maintain their stronghold at home. The opening game of this series will set the tone, and both sides will want to strike early. Will India’s refreshed squad capitalize on their T20I momentum, or will the determined West Indies Women hit back hard? Either way, all signs point to another cracking series opener!
